- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, reduce forecasted price targets to avoid over-optimism.  
- If model shows sharp upward spikes followed by high sentiment (e.g., 1.00), cap the overshoot by applying a 10–15% downward correction in the next 3–5 periods.  
- In high-sentiment environments (≥0.67), model tends to overestimate; apply a 5–10% downward bias to forecasted mean.  
- When sentiment turns negative (e.g., -0.33 or 0.00), model often fails to adjust downward; force a 5–10% downward correction in the next 5–7 periods.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 data points show strong downward momentum, apply a mean-reversion bias toward prior 10-day average.  
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and model is trending upward, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to avoid over-leveraging momentum.  
- In cases where true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >15% gap), assume sentiment was overconfident; apply a 10–15% downward adjustment to next forecast.
